title: Grouping methods
body: The mechanics of the console [grouping methods](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#grouping) `group()`, `groupEnd()`, and `groupCollapsed()` are pretty straightforward and fairly consistent between implementations (have not tested edge) with the exception of Node (not implemented) and Firefox (shipping collapsible groups in [v54](https://bugzilla.mozilla.org/show_bug.cgi?id=1088360#c35)). I'm concerned with how Printing is done inside of a group, and how we might describe it. While thinking about how I might implement this in the reference implementation, I came up with something nearly identical to [this](https://github.com/Rich-Harris/node-console-group/blob/master/src/index.js#L7) module which implements the grouping methods (with the exception of `groupCollapsed()`) in Node. It works by maintaining a `prefix` that is modified when grouping functions are called, and is prepended to data before it is printed. With that being said, I'm thinking we need to include some rhetoric in [Printer](https://console.spec.whatwg.org/#printer) that briefly explains the idea of a prefix that is prepended messages before they get printed. It is probably worth mentioning that the prefix is initially empty. Similarly, for the grouping methods we can include language explaining how the prefix is modified on calls to `group()` and `groupEnd()`. Should we explain that when a group creation method is called, all future Printing is focused inside of a newly created potentially-collapsible representation of an indented group whose members all share the same prefix? The exact characters these methods append to the prefix is *too* specific I think, since it seems to be an implementation-dependent way of indicating indentation: Chrome: FF: Safari: I also propose that if an environment does not support collapsible groups, that the behavior of `groupCollapsed()` is the same as `group()`. This is partially due to historical reasons, as Firefox has done this for pretty much as long as `group()` has been supported, and so that Node can still support calls to this method without throwing. My next concern is the default group label if none is provided. Do we simply make it the name of the function called as Chrome does, or an empty string as Firefox and Safari do? Thoughts? Some useful code I used while writing this up: https://jsbin.com/tutiho/edit?js,console
